quest.title: Flower, Feathers, and Bullets
quest.description: As the Ballistic Deduction drill nears its end, Chevreuse and Chasca seem to have reached some sort of consensus...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Deal? What deal? Did Paimon miss something important?

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: The formal phrasing would be: confirming the signature on a memorandum —

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: The "Joint Training Memorandum on Improving Shooter Effectiveness."

dialogues.speaker: Chevreuse
dialogues.text: On reflection, recruiting Miss Chasca to the Special Patrol would mean an incalculable loss of talent for her homeland of Natlan — not the wisest move.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: And the Special Patrol's clockwork-stable functioning would be unimaginable without Captain Chevreuse's daily command and coordination. Without her, Fontaine would run into no shortage of trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Chasca
dialogues.text: ...We need an unprecedented form of cooperation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is this astonishing telepathy going on...

choices.text: The two experts' minds have lined up.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: In short, after consulting with Captain Chevreuse, we've decided to start a "long-term study exchange of representatives" within three months.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: This plan can strengthen cooperation between the Special Patrol, the Flower-Feather Clan, and the Knights of Favonius — while keeping the burden as low as possible.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...In the literal sense of those words?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You'll send people back and forth — Flower-Feather Clan warriors stay in Fontaine for a stretch, and Special Patrol fighters head off to Natlan?

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Exactly. Though in practice, it's not as simple as just "letting people from each side go live in the other country."

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: The selection of the representatives, the lodging, the daily curriculum, the simulation training and live drill schedules, the budget arrangements... every detail needs systematic planning.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: And we'll be focused on the weak spots — addressing each with its own specific remedy. For instance, the Natlanese warriors don't pay much attention to formation theory, and the Fontainian shooters have almost no live experience with movement-against-movement marksmanship...

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: ...So we'll have the Natlanese warriors work in disciplined squad-level units; and we'll have the Qucusaurs grab the Special Patrol shooters by the shoulders, fly them low, and have them shoot at intercepting targets.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That sounds way too strict!

choices.text: If you can actually pull it off, the results would be tremendous.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: Many of the planned courses also rely on excellent equipment from our Mondstadt allies. Representatives from the Knights of Favonius are essential, and any results from the program should be shared with them.

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: Ahem! Captain Chevreuse, that's most thoughtful of you. Once again, our thanks for your generous offer!

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: In this drill, the observation grenades and the suite of equipment all performed normally. We'll continue regular deliveries per the existing procurement contract.

response.speaker: Hedwig
response.text: As for sending representatives for study, please let me convey this back to our headquarters, so that the officers can issue a formal reply.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: I'll provide you with the formal written documentation. I'll be waiting for good news from you.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: And to close — the topic should return to our "Ballistic Wargame."

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Captain Chevreuse is uncommonly pleased with this round's results, after all.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: #Yes. With your remarkable control-group performance to compare against, {NICKNAME}, our final piece of the puzzle is in place.

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: This drill has produced a wealth of ballistic-planning thinking samples, covering shooters of every skill level —

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: — Enough to substantially improve the original musket marksmanship textbooks, and even the instructor manuals for shooter training. Efficiency could be raised severalfold.

choices.text: Feel free to call me in for the next wargame.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: That's just what I was waiting to hear.

response.speaker: Chasca
response.text: Rest assured — I'll send you a letter the moment the time comes!

response.speaker: Chevreuse
response.text: With the marksmanship talent you're showing, you ought to be sitting on the test-setter's side of the table next time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Haha! Helping our friends in Mondstadt, Fontaine, and Natlan all get stronger is the best feeling there is!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If one day Paimon hears that the books we helped put together produced an amazing warrior, and that warrior drove off the monsters with a few quick shots, keeping everybody safe...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...That feeling would be just as good as scaring the bad guys off ourselves. Proud and grounded all at once!

choices.text: I'd be glad to take part in another exercise like this one.
Targeted training of weak points is the most effective method, after all.
They've found a plan that works for both of them.
